Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a loaf pan.
Mash the bananas and stir in the butter, sugar and egg.
Fold in the flour and baking soda, pour into the pan and bake for 60 minutes.
Simmer the chicken in the broth for 20 minutes, then shred it.
Add the carrots and celery and cook for 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the noodles, cook 8 minutes, and season to taste.
Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and olives in a large bowl.
Top with feta, drizzle with olive oil and toss gently before serving.
Brown the beef in a skillet over medium heat and drain the fat.
Stir in the seasoning with a splash of water and simmer for 5 minutes.
Fill the tortillas with beef, lettuce and cheese and serve right away.
Whisk the dry ingredients together in a bowl.
Whisk in the milk, egg and butter until just combined.
Cook ladlefuls on a hot greased griddle until bubbles form, then flip.
Cream the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Mix in the flour and fold in the chocolate chips.
Drop spoonfuls on a baking sheet and bake at 375°F for 10 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and garlic in salted water until very tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain well and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice in a bowl.
Stir in the onion, cilantro and jalapeno and season with salt.
Crush the strawberries in a heavy pot and stir in the sugar and lemon juice.
Bring to a rolling boil and cook, stirring often, until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Ladle into clean jars and seal.
Stir the sugar into one cup of hot water until it dissolves.
Mix with the lemon juice and the rest of the cold water and serve over ice.
Toss the beef in flour and brown it in batches in a large pot.
Add the broth and onion, cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrots and cook 30 minutes more until tender.
Chop the romaine and place it in a large bowl.
Add the dressing, croutons and parmesan and toss to coat.
Cook the onion and garlic in oil until soft, then brown the beef.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 30 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti, drain and toss with the sauce.
Toss the apples with the sugar, flour and cinnamon.
Pour into the bottom crust, dot with butter and cover with the top crust.
Bake at 425°F for 45 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Toss the vegetables with the oil and salt on a sheet pan.
Roast at 425°F for 25 minutes, stirring halfway, until browned.
Halve the eggs and scoop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise and mustard and spoon back into the whites.
Sprinkle with paprika and chill until serving.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Mix in the flour, oil and salt and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour before shaping.
Beat the butter and sugar, then add the eggs one at a time.
Mix in the flour, milk and vanilla until smooth.
Fill lined muffin cups two thirds full and bake at 350°F for 20 minutes.
Scramble the eggs in a buttered skillet until just set.
Divide the eggs, sausage, cheese and salsa among the tortillas and roll up tightly.
Melt the butter and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and broth and simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cream and basil.
